questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
questions.explanation: With a singular third-person subject ('She'), use 'doesn't' + base form of the verb ('like'). 'Doesn't likes' is incorrect because 'does' already carries the tense.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the correct verb tense?
options: I have seen that movie yesterday.
I had saw that movie yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Yesterday' indicates a completed past action, so simple past tense ('saw') is correct. 'Have seen' (present perfect) does not work with a specific past time reference.

questions.question: Identify the error in this sentence: "The group of students are going on a field trip."
questions.explanation: 'Group' is a collective noun and takes a singular verb. The correct form is 'The group of students is going on a field trip.' The phrase 'of students' is a prepositional phrase, not the subject.

questions.question: Which pronoun correctly completes the sentence? "Between you and ___, this is the best option."
questions.explanation: 'Between' is a preposition and takes the objective case. 'Between you and me' is correct. 'Between you and I' is a common error.

questions.question: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: Neither the teacher nor the students was present.
Neither the teacher nor the students were present.
Neither the teacher nor the students is present.
Neither the teacher nor the students has been present.
questions.correctAnswer: Neither the teacher nor the students were present.
questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the noun closest to it. 'Students' is plural, so use 'were.' This is the proximity rule for correlative conjunctions.

questions.question: Choose the sentence with the correct modifier placement.
options: She almost drove the car for six hours.
She drove almost the car for six hours.
She drove the car for almost six hours.
Almost she drove the car for six hours.
questions.correctAnswer: She drove the car for almost six hours.
questions.explanation: 'Almost' should modify 'six hours,' not 'drove' or 'the car.' The modifier must be placed next to the word it modifies to avoid ambiguity.
questions.source: Purdue OWL — Dangling and Misplaced Modifiers

questions.question: Which sentence uses the semicolon correctly?
options: I love reading; writing is my passion.
I love reading, writing; is my passion.
questions.correctAnswer: I love reading; writing is my passion.
questions.explanation: A semicolon connects two independent clauses (complete sentences). 'I love reading' and 'Writing is my passion' are both independent clauses. A semicolon should not separate a dependent clause.

questions.question: Which sentence demonstrates correct parallel structure?
options: She likes swimming, to run, and biking.
She likes swimming, running, and biking.
She likes to swim, running, and to bike.
She likes swimming, to run, and to bike.
questions.correctAnswer: She likes swimming, running, and biking.
questions.explanation: Parallel structure requires all items in a series to use the same grammatical form. 'Swimming, running, and biking' are all gerunds (-ing forms), making the structure parallel.

questions.question: Identify the error: "The data shows that the new policy is effective."
questions.explanation: 'Data' is the plural of 'datum' and traditionally takes a plural verb: 'The data show.' However, in modern usage, 'data' is increasingly treated as singular in informal contexts. In formal/exam English, the plural form is expected.
questions.source: Purdue OWL — Count and Noncount Nouns

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Who did you give the book to?
Whom did you give the book to?
To who did you give the book?
Whom did you give the book?
questions.correctAnswer: Whom did you give the book to?
questions.explanation: 'Whom' is the objective case and should be used as the object of the verb or preposition. Here, 'whom' is the indirect object of 'give.' In formal English, 'To whom did you give the book?' is also correct.

questions.question: Which word correctly completes the sentence? "There ___ many reasons to study."
questions.explanation: 'Reasons' is plural, so the plural verb 'are' is required. 'There is' would be used with a singular subject: 'There is a reason to study.'

questions.question: Which sentence is written in the passive voice?
options: The proposal was approved by the committee.
The committee will approve the proposal.
The committee has approved the proposal.
questions.correctAnswer: The proposal was approved by the committee.
questions.explanation: In passive voice, the subject receives the action. The active equivalent is 'The committee approved the proposal.' Passive voice uses a form of 'to be' + past participle.
questions.source: Purdue OWL — Active and Passive Voice

questions.question: Identify the sentence with the correct use of the subjunctive mood.
questions.explanation: The subjunctive mood expresses wishes, hypotheticals, or conditions contrary to fact. 'Were' is used for all persons in subjunctive constructions: 'I wish I were,' 'If I were you.' This is a commonly tested grammar point.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: Each of the students have submitted their homework.
Each of the students has submitted their homework.
Each of the students have submitted his or her homework.
Each of the students has submitted his or her homework.
questions.correctAnswer: Each of the students has submitted his or her homework.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular and takes a singular verb ('has'). The pronoun should also be singular and agree in gender. 'His or her' is the traditional formal choice; 'their' as singular is increasingly accepted but less formal.

questions.question: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
questions.explanation: 'It's' (with apostrophe) is the contraction of 'it is.' 'Its' (no apostrophe) is the possessive form. This is one of the most commonly confused punctuation rules in English.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the correct verb form after 'than'?
options: She runs faster than I run.
She runs faster than me run.
questions.explanation: In formal English, 'than' is a conjunction and should be followed by the subject pronoun 'I' (as in 'than I do/run'). 'Than me' is common in informal speech but considered incorrect in formal writing and exams.

questions.question: Identify the sentence with correct article usage.
questions.explanation: Use 'an' before words that begin with a vowel sound. Although 'honest' starts with 'h,' the 'h' is silent, so the word begins with a vowel sound. 'An honest' is correct.

questions.question: Which uses the correct plural form?
questions.explanation: 'Child' has an irregular plural: 'children.' There is no form 'childrens' or 'childs.' Other common irregular plurals include: man/men, woman/women, mouse/mice.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the comma correctly?
options: I went to the store, and bought milk.
I went to the store and bought milk.
I went to the store and, bought milk.
I went, to the store and bought milk.
questions.correctAnswer: I went to the store and bought milk.
questions.explanation: No comma is needed before 'and' when it connects a compound predicate (two verbs sharing the same subject: 'I went...and bought'). A comma is needed only when 'and' joins two independent clauses.

questions.question: Which demonstrates correct subject-verb agreement?
options: The number of applicants are increasing.
A number of applicants is increasing.
The number of applicants is increasing.
A number of applicants are increasing.
questions.correctAnswer: The number of applicants is increasing.
questions.explanation: 'The number' is always singular ('The number is increasing'). 'A number' is always plural ('A number of applicants are waiting'). This is a commonly tested distinction in formal grammar exams.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: "The meeting will start ___ 3:00 PM."
questions.explanation: 'At' is used for specific times: at 3:00 PM, at noon, at midnight. 'In' is for months/years/seasons. 'On' is for days and dates. This is a fundamental preposition usage rule.

questions.question: Identify the correctly structured sentence.
options: Having finished the exam, the room was left by the students.
Having finished the exam, the students left the room.
Having finished the exam, leaving the room happened.
The students having finished the exam, the room was left.
questions.correctAnswer: Having finished the exam, the students left the room.
questions.explanation: A participial phrase at the beginning of a sentence must modify the subject. 'Having finished the exam' correctly modifies 'the students.' The first option is a dangling modifier (the room didn't finish the exam).

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If I was you, I would accept the offer.
If I were you, I would accept the offer.
If I am you, I would accept the offer.
If I will be you, I would accept the offer.
questions.correctAnswer: If I were you, I would accept the offer.
questions.explanation: This is a second conditional (unreal/hypothetical situation). Use 'were' for all persons in the if-clause. 'Was' is common in informal speech but incorrect in formal English and standard exams.

questions.question: Which sentence avoids the comma splice error?
options: I love to read, I go to the library every week.
I love to read I go to the library every week.
I love to read; I go to the library every week.
I love to read, and, I go to the library every week.
questions.correctAnswer: I love to read; I go to the library every week.
questions.explanation: A comma splice joins two independent clauses with only a comma. Fixes include: using a semicolon, adding a conjunction ('I love to read, so I go...'), or splitting into two sentences.

questions.question: Which is correct?
options: Me and my friend went to the park.
My friend and I went to the park.
I and my friend went to the park.
My friend and me went to the park.
questions.correctAnswer: My friend and I went to the park.
questions.explanation: Use 'I' as the subject of a sentence. 'Me' is an object pronoun. Also, as a matter of courtesy, mention the other person first ('My friend and I,' not 'I and my friend').

questions.question: Choose the word that is most similar in meaning to 'benevolent'.
questions.explanation: 'Benevolent' means well-meaning, generous, and kindly. 'Kind' is the closest synonym. 'Malevolent' means evil or harmful — the opposite. 'Hostile' means unfriendly, and 'Indifferent' means unconcerned.

questions.question: Choose the word that is most nearly opposite in meaning to 'abundant'.
questions.explanation: 'Abundant' means existing in large quantities. 'Scarce' means in short supply — the direct antonym. 'Plentiful,' 'Ample,' and 'Copious' are all synonyms of abundant.

questions.question: The word 'ephemeral' most nearly means:
questions.explanation: 'Ephemeral' means lasting for a very short time; transitory. 'Temporary' is the closest synonym. 'Permanent' and 'Eternal' are antonyms.

questions.question: Choose the synonym of 'ubiquitous'.
questions.explanation: 'Ubiquitous' means present, appearing, or found everywhere. Something ubiquitous is omnipresent. 'Rare' and 'Unique' are near-antonyms.

questions.question: What does 'meticulous' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Meticulous' means very careful and precise, showing great attention to detail. A meticulous person takes extreme care with their work.

questions.question: Which word means 'to make a situation worse'?
questions.explanation: 'Exacerbate' means to make a problem, situation, or feeling worse. 'Ameliorate,' 'Alleviate,' and 'Mitigate' all mean to make something better or less severe — they are antonyms.

questions.question: Choose the antonym of 'generous'.
questions.explanation: 'Generous' means willing to give more than expected. 'Stingy' means unwilling to give or share — the direct opposite. 'Kind,' 'Giving,' and 'Helpful' are related to being generous.

questions.question: The word 'pragmatic' most nearly means:
questions.explanation: 'Pragmatic' means dealing with things sensibly and realistically, based on practical rather than theoretical considerations. A pragmatic person focuses on what works.

questions.question: Which word means 'to calm or pacify'?
questions.explanation: 'Appease' means to calm, satisfy, or pacify someone by giving in to their demands. 'Provoke,' 'Aggravate,' and 'Incite' all mean to stir up or worsen a situation — antonyms.

questions.question: Choose the synonym of 'verbose'.
questions.explanation: 'Verbose' means using or expressed in more words than are needed. 'Wordy' is the direct synonym. 'Concise' means brief and to the point — the opposite.

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'resilient'?
questions.explanation: 'Resilient' means able to withstand or recover quickly from difficult conditions. A resilient person bounces back from setbacks. 'Fragile' and 'Weak' are antonyms.

questions.question: Which word means 'present but not visible or active'?
questions.explanation: 'Latent' means existing but not yet developed, manifest, or active. A latent talent is one that hasn't been discovered yet. 'Manifest,' 'Obvious,' and 'Apparent' mean clearly visible — antonyms.

questions.question: Choose the antonym of 'temporary'.
questions.explanation: 'Temporary' means lasting for a limited time. 'Permanent' means lasting indefinitely — the direct antonym. 'Brief,' 'Short,' and 'Passing' are synonyms.

questions.question: The word 'candid' most nearly means:
questions.explanation: 'Candid' means truthful and straightforward; frank. A candid person speaks openly and honestly. 'Deceptive' and 'Secretive' are antonyms.

questions.question: Which word means 'to deliberately destroy or obstruct'?
questions.explanation: 'Sabotage' means to deliberately destroy, damage, or obstruct something. 'Facilitate,' 'Assist,' and 'Promote' all mean to help or support — antonyms.

questions.question: Choose the synonym of 'diligent'.
questions.explanation: 'Diligent' means having or showing careful and persistent effort. 'Hardworking' is the closest synonym. 'Lazy' and 'Careless' are antonyms.

questions.question: What does 'ambiguous' mean?
options: Open to more than one interpretation
questions.correctAnswer: Open to more than one interpretation
questions.explanation: 'Ambiguous' means having more than one possible meaning or interpretation. Ambiguous statements can be understood in multiple ways. 'Clear' and 'Precise' are antonyms.

questions.question: Choose the antonym of 'loathe'.
questions.explanation: 'Loathe' means to feel intense dislike or disgust. 'Adore' means to love deeply — the antonym. 'Hate,' 'Despise,' and 'Detest' are synonyms.

questions.question: Which word means 'excessively flattering or ingratiating'?
questions.explanation: 'Obsequious' means excessively attentive or submissive, often to gain favor. It describes someone who flatters too much. 'Sincere,' 'Genuine,' and 'Honest' are near-antonyms.

questions.question: The word 'concise' most nearly means:
questions.explanation: 'Concise' means giving a lot of information clearly and in few words. A concise explanation is short but complete. 'Lengthy' and 'Repetitive' are near-antonyms.

questions.question: Read the passage and answer: 'The Philippine Civil Service was established to ensure that government positions are awarded based on merit rather than political connections. The system aims to professionalize the civil service and improve the delivery of public services.' What is the main purpose of the Civil Service system?
options: To award positions based on merit
questions.correctAnswer: To award positions based on merit
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly states that the Civil Service was established 'to ensure that government positions are awarded based on merit.' This is the main idea of the passage.

questions.question: Based on the passage: 'Climate change affects the Philippines through stronger typhoons, rising sea levels, and increased temperatures. These changes threaten agriculture, infrastructure, and coastal communities.' What is the primary concern raised in this passage?
options: Impact of climate change on the Philippines
questions.correctAnswer: Impact of climate change on the Philippines
questions.explanation: The passage focuses on how climate change specifically affects the Philippines through typhoons, sea levels, and temperatures, and what those impacts threaten. This is the main topic.

questions.question: From the passage: 'Although the policy was well-intentioned, its implementation faced significant challenges due to lack of funding, insufficient training of personnel, and resistance from local officials.' What can be inferred about the policy?
options: The policy was a complete failure
The policy had good intentions but poor execution
questions.correctAnswer: The policy had good intentions but poor execution
questions.explanation: The passage says the policy was 'well-intentioned' but faced 'significant challenges.' This implies the policy had good goals but struggled in implementation. This is an inference — reading between the lines.

questions.question: Read the sentence: 'The diligent student reviewed her notes every evening, completed all assignments on time, and actively participated in class discussions.' Which word best describes the student?
questions.explanation: The word 'diligent' directly means hardworking, and the actions described (reviewing notes, completing assignments, participating) all support this characterization.

questions.question: Paragraph: 'The Philippines has over 7,000 islands, each with unique ecosystems. However, many of these islands face environmental threats from overfishing, deforestation, and pollution. Conservation efforts are underway but require more support.' What is the tone of this paragraph?
questions.explanation: The paragraph acknowledges threats ('environmental threats') but also notes that 'conservation efforts are underway.' This conveys concern about the situation with some hope for improvement.

questions.question: Which sentence best summarizes this passage? 'Studies show that regular exercise improves mental health by reducing anxiety and depression. Physical activity releases endorphins, which are natural mood elevators. Even 30 minutes of walking daily can make a significant difference.'
options: Exercise is only for physical health
Regular physical activity positively affects mental health
Walking is the only effective exercise
questions.correctAnswer: Regular physical activity positively affects mental health
questions.explanation: The passage's main point is that exercise improves mental health. It supports this by explaining endorphins and giving the example of walking. The other options misrepresent the passage.

questions.question: From the passage: 'The government's decision to invest in renewable energy was met with both praise and criticism. Supporters argued it was necessary for long-term sustainability, while critics pointed to the high initial costs.' What is the structure of this passage?
questions.explanation: The passage presents two opposing viewpoints: supporters (praise) and critics (criticism). This is a classic compare-and-contrast structure showing both sides of an issue.

questions.question: Which statement is a fact rather than an opinion?
options: The Philippines is the best country in Asia.
Manila is the capital of the Philippines.
Filipino food is the most delicious.
questions.correctAnswer: Manila is the capital of the Philippines.
questions.explanation: A fact can be proven true or false. 'Manila is the capital of the Philippines' is a verifiable fact. The other statements are opinions — they express personal beliefs or preferences.

questions.question: In the sentence: 'Despite the heavy rain, the dedicated volunteers continued their relief operations without complaint.' What does the word 'despite' indicate?
questions.explanation: 'Despite' is a preposition meaning 'in spite of' or 'regardless of.' It shows contrast: the volunteers continued even though there was heavy rain. This is a transition word indicating concession.

questions.question: Read: 'If the Philippines is to become a knowledge-based economy, its educational system must prioritize critical thinking over rote memorization. Current curricula emphasize recall of facts rather than application of concepts.' What does the author recommend?
options: Shifting focus from memorization to critical thinking
questions.correctAnswer: Shifting focus from memorization to critical thinking
questions.explanation: The author states that the system 'must prioritize critical thinking over rote memorization.' This is a direct recommendation. The word 'must' signals what the author believes should happen.

questions.question: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: "The speaker's arguments were so ___ that even her opponents were convinced."
questions.explanation: 'Compelling' means convincing or persuasive. If even opponents were convinced, the arguments must have been very persuasive. 'Weak,' 'Boring,' and 'Confusing' would not convince opponents.

questions.question: What does the idiom 'to burn the midnight oil' mean?
options: To work late into the night
questions.correctAnswer: To work late into the night
questions.explanation: 'To burn the midnight oil' means to work or study late into the night. The idiom originates from the time when oil lamps were used for light, and staying up late meant burning oil.

questions.question: The phrase 'a blessing in disguise' refers to:
options: Something that seems bad but turns out to be good
questions.correctAnswer: Something that seems bad but turns out to be good
questions.explanation: 'A blessing in disguise' is something that initially appears negative or unlucky but ultimately results in something positive. It's a very common idiom in both casual and formal contexts.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: "The committee's decision was ___ upon receiving new evidence that contradicted the earlier testimony."
questions.explanation: If new evidence contradicted the earlier testimony, the committee would likely change or 'reverse' its decision. 'Upheld' means to maintain the same decision, which contradicts the logic of new opposing evidence.

questions.question: What does 'to beat around the bush' mean?
options: To avoid talking about the main topic
questions.correctAnswer: To avoid talking about the main topic
questions.explanation: 'To beat around the bush' means to avoid addressing the main point or to talk indirectly about something. Someone who beats around the bush doesn't get straight to the point.

questions.question: Paragraph organization: (1) The Philippines is one of the world's most disaster-prone countries. (2) Typhoons, earthquakes, and volcanic eruptions frequently affect the archipelago. (3) The government has established disaster preparedness programs. (4) These include early warning systems and evacuation protocols. What is the correct sequence?
questions.explanation: The logical sequence is: general statement (1), supporting details/examples (2), government response (3), specific measures (4). This follows a general-to-specific organizational pattern.

questions.question: Complete: "Despite his ___ preparation, he still felt nervous before the examination."
questions.explanation: 'Despite' signals a contrast. If he was still nervous, it's surprising because he prepared thoroughly. 'Inadequate' and 'Hasty' would make nervousness expected — no contrast.

questions.question: The idiom 'to leave no stone unturned' means:
questions.explanation: 'To leave no stone unturned' means to search thoroughly or make every possible effort to achieve something. It implies exhaustive effort, turning over every stone to find what you're looking for.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: "The teacher asked the students to ___ the instructions carefully before starting the exam."
questions.explanation: 'Asked the students to' is followed by the base form of the verb. 'To read' is correct. This is the infinitive form after 'ask someone to do something.'

questions.question: Which sentence does NOT belong in this paragraph? (1) Reading improves vocabulary. (2) It also enhances critical thinking skills. (3) Many people enjoy watching movies instead. (4) Furthermore, reading reduces stress.
questions.explanation: The paragraph is about the benefits of reading. Sentence 3 shifts to a different topic (watching movies) and doesn't support the main idea. This tests the ability to identify irrelevant sentences.
